editorial:
Imagine finding out your husband, who died by suicide six years ago, was actually just murdered last week. That is the wild ride you get with Jean Bruckner. You will feel her shock as she realizes her entire life for the last few years has been a lie. The movie has a cool, mysterious vibe that makes you feel like you are solving a puzzle right along with her. As she teams up with a private investigator and flies to Chicago, you get a sense of dread because you know someone is watching her every move. It is a great setup that keeps you questioning who to trust.

The acting is solid and the twists keep the story moving fast, though some parts feel a bit like a typical TV movie. You might find some plot points a little convenient, but the suspense makes up for it. If you love a good whodunit, you should definitely check this out. It looks great if you can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but renting it on Apple TV is a quick way to watch it tonight. If you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is a smart move for a movie this gripping.
endingExplained: You find out that the husband did not kill himself years ago but faked his death to start a secret life. He was involved in a dangerous scheme that eventually caught up to him, leading to his actual murder. Jean discovers the killer is someone close to the secret circle. After a tense showdown, the truth comes out and the murderer is finally caught, giving Jean the closure she never got six years prior.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves mystery stories with big twists.
